cohort: 300 pregnant women with meconium-stained amniotic fluid and a control group of 100 pregnant women with clear amniotic fluid, the majority of whom were between 21-30 years old and at 37-40 weeks gestation.
finding: The incidence of non-reassuring fetal heart rate patterns, cesarean section rates, low Apgar scores, neonatal admissions, and perinatal mortality were significantly higher in women with meconium-stained amniotic fluid and non-reactive non-stress tests (NSTs).
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in the MSAF group (52.7%) compared to the control group (37%), and even higher in the thick meconium subgroup, irrespective of NST results.
